additional_info.subject: RE: ID0484437-DC/Si-D/PL-[MP / ND 170000071] Station offline in backend system CRM:03056001126
additional_info.body:
Dear Poland Service Team,
I am reaching out in regards of this ticket
ID0484437
for OCPP Backend disconnection on charger
MP/ND 170000071.
Apologies for the late reply.
I checked the logs and analyzed the OCPP disconnection. Here is my analysis:
The connection to the Backend went offline at 2026-03-14T06:24:28.
The charger has an embedded retry mechanism to ensure reconnection (websocket ping interval) every 30 seconds. This results in the connection being re-established every 30 seconds, but as you mentioned it disconnected immediately every time.
The connection to the Backend was finally re-established on its own at 2026-03-16T13:04:08.
I saw that several reboots were performed on 2026-03-16 morning, but these did not restore the connection immediately.
I did not find a clear reason why the OCPP connection went offline, neither why the connection was re-established on its own. I checked the network connection strength of router 2 around the events of disconnection and connection, but could not notice any significant difference:
For example: 2
026-03-16T13:02:00.764484+00:00 [FW070006G1] sicharge-cp [local0:info] sicharge-cp-backend/f316976fb3fd[738]: [ensureOCPPConnection] router2 - signal strength: {"stdout":"+QCSQ: \"LTE\",77,-108,98,-11\r\n\r\n","stderr":""}
108 is the
RSRP (Reference Signal Received Power, signal strength). All samples are in the "Fair to Poor" category according to LTE standards (categories: Excellent > -80, Good > -90, Fair > -100, Poor ≤ -100)
11 is the RSRQ (Reference Signal Received Quality). All samples are also "Good" by LTE standards (categories: Excellent > -10, Good > -15, Poor ≤ -15)
Did you receive by any chance any feedback from CPO Backend side? From charger side I cannot find a reason for this disconnection. I performed an analysis over the month of March, and checked that the OCPP connection went offline only in this occasion in the full month. I would then assume the issue could be related either to a temporary issue from Backend side, or to a temporary issue of the network provider.
With R&D we are investigating OCPP disconnections which appear with a different symptom compared to this one and are common to more chargers. If you agree, I would proceed to close this ticket as the event happened only once and solved on its own. I would recommend to check the disconnection event with Backend CPO and open a new ticket if the behavior happens again on this charger on on others.
Awaiting for your feedback before closing the ticket.
With kind regards,
Fosco Servidei
Siemens AG
